Subject: Recap + next steps — pricing & latency tradeoffs

Thanks for the call this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same frame: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary product area: real-time customer support assistant + transaction summarization.
- Projected volume (12mo ramp): 50–120M tokens/month (expect steady-state around ~100M).
- Typical prompt/response size: ~150 tokens in / ~250 tokens out (roughly 400 tokens per interaction).
- Concurrency: expected peaks ~30–50 concurrent active users; steady CRUC about 10–20 qps.
- UX SLO: p95 latency target ~400–500ms for the chat experience; willing to consider streaming to improve perceived latency.
- Compliance: SOC2 required; some discussion about Private/VPC for regulated flows later.
- Budget: given internal procurement ranges, the target budget band is roughly $8k–$15k/month. You mentioned aiming for a target unit price in the ~$80–$150 / 1M tokens range — call that ballpark for qualification.

Latency vs cost tradeoffs we discussed:
- Hosted (standard) is fastest to start, simpler to operate; unit cost a bit higher.
- Dedicated/reserved capacity gives lower per-token unit economics but comes with a monthly reserved fee and commit. Better if you need predictable p95 at scale.
- Batching (continuous batching) lowers per-token cost but increases tail latency; streaming reduces perceived latency for long responses but can slightly increase compute overhead per token.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I'll send a short cost scenarios doc with two concrete scenarios (Hosted vs Dedicated) and estimated monthly cost at 50M / 100M / 120M tokens.
2) Rishi will join a follow-up to review SLA / Dedicated sizing and pilot options — propose Wed or Thu next week.
3) If you can confirm the tighter targets (exact p95 SLO and final monthly budget target) we can include an SLO premium option in the quote.

Attachments I'll include in the next email: cost_estimate_v1.xlsx, high-level SLA_options.pdf.

Thanks — spoke soon.
—

Thanks — adding the batching/streaming line items and SLO options now. High level notes while I build the spreadsheet: 

Unit economics (rough, for modeling):
- Hosted (standard): $140 / 1M tokens (baseline, includes managed autoscaling and 30-day retention).
- Hosted + SLO premium (p95 target <500ms): add ~20% premium ($168 / 1M tokens) — this is an example of an SLO-backed pricing band we can offer for mission-critical routes.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): $85 / 1M tokens (assuming a monthly reserved commitment) + a baseline reserved quota fee. Example reserved starter tier: $7,500/month reserved capacity (includes minimum throughput and 24/7 priority support).

How batching/streaming affects cost and latency (general guidance):
- Batching (continuous batching): reduces per-token compute cost by ~10–30% depending on sequence length and batch hit rate. However, aggressive batching raises p95 because requests wait to form batches. We can tune batching windows — smaller windows give lower latency with less cost savings.
- Streaming: reduces perceived latency for end users (start-of-response comes sooner), can shave 100–300ms off perceived p95 on long responses. Streaming does not necessarily change per-token cost materially for most models; in some runtimes it increases CPU overhead by ~5–10% due to incremental send/flush logic.
- Caching/prefix-KV caching: for repeat contexts (like assistant prompts), this can reduce compute by up to 40% for cached prefixes.

I'll attach a scenario sheet that shows Hosted vs Dedicated at 50M / 100M / 120M tokens with and without a 20% batching improvement. Also include two SLO bands: standard (<800ms) and premium (<500ms) so procurement can see both line-items.

Sending the spreadsheet and SLA doc in the next message.

Marissa
